hypothesis: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027のcash-conversion低下は主に一時的なaccounts-receivable buildであり、Q2 ending AR intensityをQ1 FY2027水準へ正規化すると、20% Data Center growth scenarioで必要なFCF marginに対するheadroomは十分に回復する。

decision_rule.use_if: Q1 revenue-scaled AR intensityへの正規化だけでfirst-half FY2027 FCF marginが20% growth scenarioのrequired FCF margin 38.421675%を5pt以上上回り、inventory/revenue ratioのQ1からQ2への悪化が2pt未満で、後続実績でAR回収またはFCF conversion改善が確認される。
decision_rule.condition_if: AR normalizationで5pt以上のheadroomが得られ、inventory intensityも大幅悪化していないが、AR回収またはFCF conversion改善の後続実績がまだ観測されていない。
decision_rule.reject_if: AR normalization後も20% growth scenarioのrequired FCF marginを満たさない、またはinventory/supply commitment増加がAR効果を上回る恒久的cash drainを示す。
decision_rule.unverified_if: NVIDIAのQ1/Q2 revenue、AR、inventory、FCF、またはcanonical required FCF marginのidentityが不足する。

capital_allocation_importance: 前回研究ではNVDAの20% growth scenarioのFCF-margin headroomが+0.8812ptしかなくAVGOを下回った。cash conversion低下がworking-capital timingならvaluation margin of safetyを過小評価しているため、ARとinventoryを分解して再評価する。
primary_sources: NVIDIA Q1 FY2027 Form 10-Q, quarter ended 2026-04-26: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000052/nvda-20260426.htm
NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q, quarter ended 2026-07-26: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm

method.point_in_time: Use only balance-sheet and cash-flow values reported through 2026-07-26 plus the existing canonical valuation hurdle. No future quarter is used.
method.ar_intensity: Compute ending AR / same-quarter revenue and an approximate 90-day DSO proxy. Normalize Q2 ending AR to the Q1 FY2027 AR/revenue ratio without altering revenue, inventory, capex or any other cash-flow item.
method.inventory_check: Compare ending inventory/revenue ratios for Q4 FY2026, Q1 FY2027 and Q2 FY2027 to distinguish proportional supply build from a sharp intensity deterioration.
method.normalized_fcf: AR-normalized H1 FCF = reported H1 FCF + (actual Q2 ending AR - Q2 revenue * Q1 AR/revenue ratio). This is a sensitivity, not reported or guided FCF.
method.benchmark: Compare reported and AR-normalized H1 FY2027 FCF margin with the canonical 20% growth required FCF margin and with H1 FY2026 realized FCF margin.
method.risk_metrics: NOT_APPLICABLE: point-in-time working-capital/fundamental valuation diagnostic, not a trading-strategy backtest.

customer_advance_context.interpretation: Customer advances increased materially while AR also rose, showing mixed working-capital timing rather than a simple demand collapse.

supply_commitment_context.interpretation: Large multi-year supply commitments are a genuine forward cash/risk exposure and prevent treating all working-capital normalization as guaranteed cash release.

benchmark_and_alternative.simple_benchmark: Reported H1 FY2027 FCF margin 39.302845% leaves only +0.881170pt headroom versus the 20% Data Center growth valuation requirement of 38.421675%.
benchmark_and_alternative.alternative_hypothesis: The margin weakness is primarily timing from extended customer payment terms rather than a structural loss of unit economics.
benchmark_and_alternative.alternative_result: SUPPORTED CONDITIONALLY: Q2 AR intensity rose from 49.88% to 65.54% of quarterly revenue while inventory intensity rose only 1.21pt. Normalizing Q2 AR to Q1 intensity increases H1 FCF margin to 47.773213%, creating +9.351538pt headroom. NVIDIA explicitly attributes H1 operating-cash-flow pressure partly to extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements.

verdict.reason: The observed cash-conversion deterioration is mechanically dominated by a sharp AR build. AR normalization alone raises H1 FCF-margin headroom from +0.8812pt to +9.3515pt, while inventory/revenue intensity increased only 1.21pt. However the cash has not yet been collected and supply/capacity commitments increased to 279B USD, so a durable recovery cannot yet be classified USE.
verdict.capital_allocation_implication: Do not treat NVDA's H1 FY2027 reported FCF margin of 39.30% as a durable cash-conversion ceiling. For the 20% growth valuation scenario, monitor AR/revenue or DSO normalization: a return toward Q1 intensity would restore substantial margin-of-safety. At the same time, keep the 279B USD supply/capacity commitment as a separate downside condition rather than netting it away against expected receivable collection.

implementation.delete_or_cleanup: No dedicated code/config/workflow/one-off script created; no cleanup required.

limitations: AR-normalized FCF is a sensitivity, not issuer-reported or guided FCF; collection timing and eventual credit losses are not known.
AR/revenue is used as a transparent quarterly intensity proxy; the approximate 90-day DSO proxy is not a fully weighted trailing-sales DSO calculation.
NVIDIA states some investment-grade customers may receive payment terms from 90 days up to one year, so Q1 AR intensity is not guaranteed to be the future steady state.
Inventory intensity is stable relative to revenue, but absolute inventory and supply/capacity commitments are rising rapidly and can create future cash or write-down risk.
The 20% Data Center growth scenario is a canonical valuation sensitivity, not NVIDIA guidance.
next_high_value_hypothesis: NVIDIAの279B USD supply/capacity commitmentsは、Data Center revenue run-rateとgross profit/cash generationに対して過大ではないか。AVGO purchase-commitment研究と同じcoverage frameworkで、期限別92B/87B/88B USD commitmentsをcash-generation capacityと比較する。
